title: London data center cooling failure
affected: Part of europe-west2-a and a subset of dependent services. Host OS and versions were not disclosed.
summary: Several redundant cooling systems failed in extreme heat. The operator shut down affected capacity to protect hardware.
symptoms: Terminated compute instances, degraded services, and networking disruption.
errors: Some Cloud Storage customers saw HTTP 500 responses.
logs: Raw facility and host logs are not published in the report.
topology: One facility hosting part of a cloud availability zone with dependent regional services.
hypotheses: A link fault alone does not explain a shared thermal alarm. Compare facilities telemetry and host power state with network symptoms.
investigation: Correlate facilities alerts and temperature with host and service health. Verify response ownership and recover dependencies in stages.
commands: Lab only: show environment, show hardware, ping srv1, kubectl get nodes.
cause: Google confirmed simultaneous failures of redundant cooling systems while outside temperatures were unusually high.
solution: Google powered down affected servers, repaired cooling, then restored services as temperatures returned to acceptable levels. Some residual customer impact took longer to clear.
alternatives: The report does not establish another successful mitigation.
rollback: Training guidance: pause restart if thermal alarms recur. Coordinate any real facilities or power work with authorized operators.
prevention: Review cooling redundancy and recovery dependencies, and rehearse staged service restoration.
evidence: Operator postmortem documents the cause and completed recovery. Simulated commands, thresholds and topology are fictional.

title: Routing policy change disrupted traffic at 19 data centers
affected: 19 Cloudflare locations. Operating systems and router software versions were not disclosed.
summary: A network configuration rollout interrupted traffic at several major sites.
symptoms: Some clients could not reach services relying on affected Cloudflare locations.
logs: The report provides an event timeline. Raw router logs were not published.
topology: Multiple sites using a shared resilient network architecture.
hypotheses: Distinguish policy-induced route withdrawal from physical link failure by checking route advertisements and change timestamps.
investigation: Correlate lost reachability with the rollout. Compare route announcements and policy ordering against the last known working configuration.
commands: Training examples: show ip route and traceroute. Production syntax varies.
cause: Cloudflare confirmed incorrect policy ordering prevented required routes from being advertised.
solution: Engineers reverted the configuration change and restored the affected data centers.
rollback: Coordinate a single revert owner per site. Validate route announcements and client traffic after reverting.
prevention: Canary changes on representative sites and use automatic rollback for unconfirmed changes.
evidence: Operator postmortem documents the cause and completed rollback.
